madonna-litta.text: she brought forth her firstborn son
madonna-litta.full: And she brought forth her firstborn son, and wrapped him in swaddling clothes, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the inn.

madonna-granduca.text: Mary kept all these things, and pondered
madonna-granduca.full: But Mary kept all these things, and pondered them in her heart.

madonna-pomegranate.text: Can a woman forget her sucking child
madonna-pomegranate.full: Can a woman forget her sucking child, that she should not have compassion on the son of her womb? yea, they may forget, yet will I not forget thee.

madonna-dove.text: As one whom his mother comforteth
madonna-dove.full: As one whom his mother comforteth, so will I comfort you; and ye shall be comforted in Jerusalem.

virgin-child-st-anne.text: which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois
virgin-child-st-anne.full: When I call to remembrance the unfeigned faith that is in thee, which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice; and I am persuaded that in thee also.

banjo-lesson.text: Train up a child in the way he should go
banjo-lesson.full: Train up a child in the way he should go: and when he is old, he will not depart from it.

tobit-anna.text: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children
tobit-anna.full: A good man leaveth an inheritance to his children’s children: and the wealth of the sinner is laid up for the just.

old-man-grandson.text: the beauty of old men is the gray head
old-man-grandson.full: The glory of young men is their strength: and the beauty of old men is the gray head.

isaac-blessing-jacob.text: Hast thou but one blessing, my father?
isaac-blessing-jacob.full: And Esau said unto his father, Hast thou but one blessing, my father? bless me, even me also, O my father. And Esau lifted up his voice, and wept.

prodigal-tavern.text: and there wasted his substance with riotous living
prodigal-tavern.full: And not many days after the younger son gathered all together, and took his journey into a far country, and there wasted his substance with riotous living.

cezanne-mother.text: Her children arise up, and call her blessed
cezanne-mother.full: Her children arise up, and call her blessed; her husband also, and he praiseth her.

orlai-mother.text: Then shall the dust return to the earth
orlai-mother.full: Then shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.

tanner-mother.text: Man that is born of a woman
tanner-mother.full: Man that is born of a woman is of few days, and full of trouble.

ensor-father.text: we see through a glass, darkly
ensor-father.full: For now we see through a glass, darkly; but then face to face: now I know in part; but then shall I know even as also I am known.

mancini-father.text: thou hast made me as the clay
mancini-father.full: Remember, I beseech thee, that thou hast made me as the clay; and wilt thou bring me into dust again?

cassatt-oval-mirror.text: even as a hen gathereth her chickens
cassatt-oval-mirror.full: O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!

cassatt-combing.text: her hair is given her for a covering
cassatt-combing.full: But if a woman have long hair, it is a glory to her: for her hair is given her for a covering.

cassatt-nurse-reading.text: from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures
cassatt-nurse-reading.full: And that from a child thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise unto salvation through faith which is in Christ Jesus.

morisot-garden.text: walking in the garden in the cool of the day
morisot-garden.full: And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day: and Adam and his wife hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God amongst the trees of the garden.

morisot-meadow.text: All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness
morisot-meadow.full: The voice said, Cry. And he said, What shall I cry? All flesh is grass, and all the goodliness thereof is as the flower of the field:

bouguereau-pieta.text: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me
bouguereau-pieta.full: My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? why art thou so far from helping me, and from the words of my roaring?

michelangelo-pieta.text: nigh unto them that are of a broken heart
michelangelo-pieta.full: The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart; and saveth such as be of a contrite spirit.

klimt-death-life.text: Thou wilt shew me the path of life
klimt-death-life.full: Thou wilt shew me the path of life: in thy presence is fulness of joy; at thy right hand there are pleasures for evermore.

munch-deathbed.text: LORD, make me to know mine end
munch-deathbed.full: LORD, make me to know mine end, and the measure of my days, what it is; that I may know how frail I am.

munch-sickroom.text: The LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing
munch-sickroom.full: The LORD will strengthen him upon the bed of languishing: thou wilt make all his bed in his sickness.
